analysis:
On 7 September 2024, campaigning for the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly elections, Shah said statehood would be restored to the Union Territory after the polls. On 8 September he said only the Central government and the Prime Minister could take the decision. In Parliament in August 2019 he had said statehood would be restored 'at an appropriate time' after normalcy.

The Assembly elections were held on 18 September, 25 September and 1 October 2024. A National Conference-led government was sworn in. As of October 2026, Jammu and Kashmir is still a Union Territory.

Omar Abdullah raised restoration again with Shah in May 2026 and September 2026. The Centre has not set a date; in October 2026 a Union Minister said the timing rested with the PM and Home Minister. The specific 2024 post-election target has therefore not been met, although the pledge itself has not been formally withdrawn.
notes: The 7 Sep 2024 report is an Akashvani summary, so the exact wording is a paraphrase. The deadline 2024-12-31 is an editorial reading of 'after the Assembly elections' (polls concluded 1 Oct 2024); Shah did not state a date. The Hindu article is undated in search results.
